predecessors.name: Dutch East India Company
predecessors.text: the VOC possessions that Cliopatria draws in 1800: Java, the Moluccas, the Lesser Sundas and parts of Sulawesi

successors.name: Republic of Indonesia
successors.text: the Indies of 1949 without the western half of New Guinea

successors.name: Dutch New Guinea
successors.text: the western half of New Guinea

ledger.x: 1800: the VOC's possessions are nationalized as the Dutch East Indies.
1800: the Pontianak sultanate is counted inside the Dutch East Indies as a protected sultanate.

1800: the Dutch state takes over the VOC's possessions ('came under the administration of the Dutch government in 1800'); that Mempawah is among them rests on the Mempawah page's Dutch-installed panembahan ('enshrined in the agreement dated 27 August 1787'), a reading, hence confidence 2.
1800: the Dutch state takes over the VOC's possessions ('came under the administration of the Dutch government in 1800').
1800: Gowa's overlord is the Dutch East Indies.
1800: the Dutch state takes over the VOC's suzerainty over Ternate.
1806: the colony passes to Louis Bonaparte's Kingdom of Holland.
1806: Yogyakarta becomes a Dutch protectorate.
1806: Surakarta becomes a Dutch protectorate.
1806: the Dutch take Tidore.
22 November 1808: Daendels absorbs the Banten Sultanate.
1810: France annexes the Kingdom of Holland and the Indies become a French colony run by Dutch officials.
1810: British forces take the Dutch Moluccas.
1811: the Dutch protectorate lapses when Britain takes Java; the infobox lists a 'Protectorate state of the British East India Company (1811-1816)'.
1811: the Dutch protectorate lapses when Britain takes Java.
1811: a sultan sits again on Tidore.
18 September 1811: Janssens surrenders Java to the British.
13 August 1814: Britain hands Bangka to the Netherlands.
13 August 1814: Dutch Malacca, Dutch Bengal (except Bernagore) and Dutch Coromandel are returned to the Netherlands by the treaty.
1816: independent Dutch control is restored.
1816: the Moluccas return to the Dutch with the restoration of 1816.
1816: Java returns to the Dutch.
1816: Dutch protectorate again.
1816: Dutch protectorate again.
1817: 'A treaty was signed in 1817 where the sultan and grandees received annual subsidies', the Dutch restoration after the British interlude.

1817: the Dutch return to the Moluccas; the Bacan page says only that the British-appointed Sultan Kamarullah (1797-1826) 'was allowed to remain after the return of the Dutch to Maluku' and that the VOC contracts of 1656 and 1667 had put Bacan 'under the…
1819: Padang returns to the Netherlands.
1819: the Dutch take control of Sambas.

c. 1820: 'When the Dutch were finally expelled from Mempawah, Gusti Jati was crowned the Sultan of Mempawah'; 'around 1820' on the page, which gives no year for the expulsion. Mirrors sultanate-of-mempawah /ledger/9. Mempawah is independent again until 1831.
April 1821: the Dutch join the adat leaders against the Padri.
June 1821: the Dutch annex Palembang.
1824: the Dutch residency of Ternate.
1824: 'In 1824, the Dutch signed the Masang Agreement ending hostilities with the state of Bonjol'.
1824: Britain withdraws its opposition to Dutch occupation of Belitung under the Treaty of London (17 March 1824).
1 March 1825: Britain hands Bencoolen to the Netherlands.
1 March 1825: the Netherlands hands Malacca to Britain (the city and fort; the Dutch agreed to open no offices on the Malay Peninsula).
1 March 1825: the Netherlands gives up all its establishments in Dutch India to Britain under the Treaty of London (transfers on 1 March 1825).
1830: after the Java War the Dutch annex the outlying mancanagara of the Javanese courts.
1830: the Surakarta share of the mancanagara (same zone as the preceding event; the Dutch also deposed Pakubuwono VI and exiled him to Ambon in 1830).
1831: Dutch intervention ends Mempawah's restored independence.

1831: the Second Padri War begins (infobox 'Second Padri War (1831-1837): Dutch victory'); 'At the beginning of August 1831, Lintau was successfully conquered and put Luhak Tanah Datar under Dutch control.'
2 May 1833: the Dutch take the heart of the Minangkabau highlands.
1834: Cliopatria adds the Sukadana sultanate's cells in West Kalimantan.
27 September 1834: Bulungan becomes a Dutch protectorate.
16 August 1837: the last Padri land passes to the Dutch.
16 August 1837: 'Fort Bonjol was completely conquered' after Tajadi Hill fell on 15 August.
1844: the Dutch take direct control of Kutai.
1846: the first Dutch military expedition against north Bali.
1849: a third Dutch intervention brings northern Bali under Dutch control ('an 1849 intervention brought northern Bali under Dutch control' after the failed expeditions of 1846 and 1848).
1849: Cliopatria adds Berau to the Indies.
1849: 'in 1849 Bangli assisted the Dutch in their military expedition against Buleleng', which 'permitted the Dutch to take control of the northern Bali kingdoms of Buleleng and Jembrana'.
1853: Cliopatria adds East and West Kalimantan land that its Sulu row had claimed.
1856: Cliopatria adds 31 cells in West and North Sumatra and Aceh with no former owner in its data.
7 October 1857: the Dutch depose the Sultan of Riau-Lingga.
1859: Cliopatria adds 18 cells in South Sulawesi (Bone's land).
20 April 1859: the Treaty of Lisbon moves the Portuguese-Dutch frontier.
1 May 1859: the Banjarmasin War begins.
1860: the Dutch abolish the Sultanate of Banjar and rule it from Batavia.
21 August 1862: Cliopatria adds the east coast of North Sumatra.
21 August 1862: Siak comes under Dutch protection.

1863: the Banjarmasin War ends in Dutch victory ('The war ended with a Dutch victory in 1863'; Hidayatullah surrendered in early 1862, Antasari died on 11 October 1862; sporadic fighting continued until 1905).
1866: Cliopatria adds 77 cells in the Lesser Sundas (73 in East Nusa Tenggara) with no former owner.
1873: Cliopatria draws the western half of New Guinea as Dutch.
26 March 1873: the Dutch attack Aceh.
April 1873: the Dutch hold the coast of Aceh, then the capital in January 1874; the rest of Aceh stays unconquered until 1904.
June 1878: the protectorate ends in annexation.
June 1878: the Dutch incorporate Bulungan (same sentence).
1889: 'At the demise of Sultan Muhammad Sadik (1862-1889) a commission of grandees governed for many years'; 'Dutch rule was represented by a controleur after 1883'.
1889: the old line ends and Bacan is governed by Dutch officials and a commission of grandees.
1894: the Dutch take Lombok.
1894: the Dutch take Karangasem.
1898: Cliopatria adds about 1,900 cells, the interior of Kalimantan (1,500), West Sumatra, Jambi and Bengkulu.
1904: the Aceh War ends in Dutch victory.
1904: Aceh passes under Dutch control.
1904: the Dutch end the Jambi Sultanate.
1905: Bima passes under direct Dutch control.
1905-1906: south-west Sulawesi is occupied.
1905: 'In 1905 Bima was turned into a "fief" (leen) and Sultan Ibrahim had to give up the rights to foreign trade'; 'Bima was subjected to indirect colonial rule from 1908 to 1949'.
1905: 'The title of sultan lapsed in 1905 and was replaced by a regency'.
1905: the regency replaces the sultan, and Tidore passes to direct Dutch control.
1905: the Dutch take Luwu.
1905: the Dutch take Wajo.
1906: the Dutch destroy the Badung royal house.
1908: Cliopatria adds the rest of Sulawesi in the sweep of 'direct colonial rule extended throughout the rest of the archipelago from 1901 to 1910'.
April 1908: the Dutch assault on Klungkung ends Balinese rule.
1911: Gowa loses its independence.
1911: the vassal sultanate becomes a Dutch East Indies regency (same sentence).
1914: the vassalage ends.
1914: the Dutch annex Ternate.
January 1942: Japan invades the Indies.
February 1942: Japanese forces land on Sumatra (month only) and, on 19 February, on Timor after taking Ambon; the Eastern Task Force.
9 March 1942: the Dutch surrender Java and the Indies fall.
1944: Allied forces liberate much of Dutch New Guinea.
1945: the Javanese principalities are disbanded.
1945: the Surakarta principality is disbanded.
May-July 1945: the Allied Borneo campaign 'was fought to liberate British and Dutch Borneo'.
15 August 1945: Japan surrenders and the Dutch East Indies pass to the UK-led South East Asia Command that day.
October 1945: British forces, with Dutch NICA troops, land in the Republic's cities.
1946: 'Sultan Syarif Kasim II, ceded his kingdom to the Republic of Indonesia in 1946 and encouraged other sultans to do likewise'.
November 1946: the Linggadjati Agreement ends the first phase.
November 1946: the Netherlands recognises the Republic as the de facto authority over Java, Madura and Sumatra at Linggadjati.
20 July 1947: the Dutch launch Operation Product against the Republic (dated 21 July-5 August).
4 August 1947: a ceasefire called for by UN Security Council resolution 27 is ordered by the Dutch and Sukarno.
August 1947: Dutch forces hold the plantation and port regions they took in Operation Product.
19 December 1948: Operation Kraai.
December 1948: the Dutch hold the Republic's cities.
27 December 1949: the fighting ends with the transfer of sovereignty.
1949: the Pontianak sultanate leaves the Dutch East Indies.
27 December 1949: Dutch New Guinea stays Dutch.
27 December 1949: the Netherlands transfers sovereignty over the Dutch East Indies to the United States of Indonesia.

wars.name: Invasion of Java (1811)
wars.outcome: The British fleet landed at Cilincing on 4 August 1811, Batavia capitulated on 8 August and Janssens surrendered on 18 September; Britain held Java and Madura until it returned them to the Dutch in 1816 under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814.

wars.name: Java War
wars.outcome: Ended on 28 March 1830 with Diponegoro's arrest; afterwards the Dutch annexed the outlying mancanagara areas of the Javanese princely states and Yogyakarta kept roughly the boundary of today's special region.

wars.name: Padri War
wars.outcome: The Dutch pushed the Padri out of Pagaruyung on 4 March 1822, conquered Lintau in August 1831, took Padang Lawas on 8 June 1835 and fully conquered Fort Bonjol on 16 August 1837, after which the Minangkabau highlands were Dutch.

wars.name: Banjarmasin War
wars.outcome: 'The war ended with a Dutch victory in 1863'; the Dutch abolished the Sultanate of Banjarmasin and ruled it 'under direct control of Batavia'.

wars.name: Aceh War
wars.outcome: The infobox dates the war 1873-1904; the Dutch took the coast in 1873, the capital in January 1874 and had 'most of Aceh' under control by the end of 1904.

wars.name: Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies
wars.outcome: Japan invaded on 10 January 1942 and the Dutch commander surrendered on 9 March 1942; the colony continued 'in exile (1942-1945)' until Japan's surrender on 15 August 1945.

wars.name: Indonesian National Revolution
wars.outcome: Linggadjati (November 1946) recognised the Republic as the de facto authority over Java, Madura and Sumatra; Operation Product (20 July 1947) and Operation Kraai (19 December 1948) took back its plantation, port and city areas; sovereignty was transferred on…

wars.name: Dutch interventions in Bali
wars.outcome: Expeditions in 1846 and 1848 failed, 'an 1849 intervention brought northern Bali under Dutch control', and Bali was 'subjugated with military conquests' in 1906 and April 1908.

certainty.note: Coasts, forts and Java were held; no page gives surveyed interior lines.
Direct colonial rule throughout the archipelago; this rests on the page's 1901-1910 sweep, not on a surveyed border list.
Occupation zones of 1942-1945 and the Republic's changing front lines of 1945-1949 are not surveyed borders.
